title: Performance evidence — written update
situation: In a technical discussion, an optimization is said to be twice as fast. You must write the decision accurately without overstating the evidence.
instructions: Write four sentences on the conditions a performance claim needs: what was measured, on what input, and how many times.

vocabulary.meaning: a measurement stated with its input, its environment, and its repetition count, without which a speed claim cannot be checked
the spread between repeated runs, which decides whether an observed difference means anything at all

expectedElements: The missing conditions of the claim are enumerated
Variance across runs is raised, not only the mean
The request is specific enough to be answered
modelAnswer: The claim of a twofold improvement cannot be evaluated as stated. I need three conditions: what was measured, whether the whole request or one function in isolation; on what input, since an optimisation that helps a large collection may do nothing at realistic sizes; and how many runs were made, with the spread between them. A single pair of runs can differ by more than the claimed factor for reasons unrelated to the change. Please share the raw measurements as evidence rather than the ratio alone.
commonMistakes: Accepting a ratio without the input size it was measured on
Comparing means without looking at the spread across runs
variants: Rewrite the update as the measurement protocol you want followed.
